newsitem.title: UK: IPE crude futures end higher in thin market.
newsitem.headline: IPE crude futures end higher in thin market.

text.p: IPE November crude futures closed 27 cents higher on Monday in thin, range-bound trading with gas oil still leading the rest of the oil complex, brokers said.

November Brent closed at $22.27 a barrel, just below the day's high of $22.29 a barrel. The contract dipped to an intra-day low of $21.83 a barrel in the afternoon session after NYMEX heating oil was dragged down by weak gasoline futures.
"It's very thin. There is a lack of depth to the market," a futures broker said.
The Jewish Yom Kippur holiday made for thin volume in New York, which some traders said explained the market's volatility.

IPE crude futures opened slightly firmer on fears over the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin but the early gains were quickly wiped out as brokers assessed there would be no impact on Russian oil exports.
With Iraq out of the news and signs the United States was considering scaling down its military presence in the Gulf, gas oil took the seasonal lead in determining price direction, dealers said.
"Brent is staying very much in a defined range and gas oil is still holding an uptrend," a futures broker said.
IPE gas oil closed $4.25 higher at $218.25 a tonne.
The weak link in the oil complex was gasoline, which dealers say has held back NYMEX heating oil.
"Gasoline and heating oil are on different planets. Crude followed gasoline at first then decided to follow heat. It took off on nothing," the broker said.
